## Motivation

`OpenAIServingRerank._handle_vl_reranker_request` (the Qwen3-VL reranker path) scores documents in a serial loop: it builds a `GenerateReqInput` for one document, awaits it, then moves to the next. The scheduler never sees more than one document of a request at a time, so latency grows linearly with the number of documents (~40 ms per document in our deployment, see below). The text Qwen3 reranker path in the same file already submits all pairs in one batch.

Each per-document request also sets `logprob_start_len=0` with `top_logprobs_num=50`, which asks the engine to compute and return top-50 logprobs for every prompt position. `_extract_score_from_logprobs` only reads `output_top_logprobs[0]`, so the input-position logprobs are discarded.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_rerank.py`:
- Move the per-document body into a local `async def _score_one(doc)` and run all documents with `asyncio.gather`, so the scheduler can batch them. `gather` preserves input order, so `scores[i]` still corresponds to `request.documents[i]`.
- Set `logprob_start_len=-1` so only the output token's logprobs are computed.
- Add `import asyncio`.

No public API change. Prompt rendering, `top_logprobs_num`, and the scoring formula are unchanged.

`test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_rerank_vl.py` (new, registered CPU test):
- All documents of a request are in flight at the same time (a serial implementation times out instead of hanging).
- Scores still map to input order when requests finish in reverse order.
- Per-document requests use `logprob_start_len=-1`.

The first and third tests fail on `main`. With this change, the new tests and the existing `test/registered/prefill_only/test_serving_rerank.py` pass (16 passed):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=99 python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_rerank_vl.py \
  test/registered/prefill_only/test_serving_rerank.py
```

`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=99` hides the GPU; an empty value currently breaks the import of `sglang.test.test_utils`.

## Accuracy Tests

Scores come from the same yes/no logprobs of the first output token. Skipping prompt logprobs does not change the label logprob gap: for a probe prompt, `logprob_start_len=0` and `-1` return yes/no logprobs of -7.748/-9.748 and -7.700/-9.700, so `p_yes / (p_yes + p_no)` is identical. On a 16-document request, the largest absolute score difference against the serial implementation is 0.012. This comes from batching changing the GPU reduction order in bf16, not from a logic change. The ranking is identical apart from the order of exact ties.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B, 1x NVIDIA L20 (shared with two other SGLang instances; reranker KV capped at 8000 tokens), `/v1/rerank`, ~60-character Chinese documents, best of 3:

| Documents | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 42.3 ms | 33.1 ms |
| 4 | 161.8 ms | 63.0 ms |
| 8 | 321.0 ms | 65.6 ms |
| 16 | 644.4 ms | 98.5 ms |

"Before" was measured on v0.5.22 and "after" on v0.5.23 with this patch; `serving_rerank.py` in v0.5.23 is identical to `main`, and `_handle_vl_reranker_request` is unchanged since v0.5.22.

## Related

#47708 fixes the label lookup on the same code path (request the yes/no token ids directly instead of searching the top-50 list). The two PRs are independent, but they touch adjacent lines of the `GenerateReqInput(...)` call. Whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase that keeps both new values (`token_ids_logprob=[...]` and `logprob_start_len=-1`). All tests of both PRs pass with that resolution. The test mock in this PR answers both `output_top_logprobs` and `output_token_ids_logprobs`, so it does not depend on the merge order.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No new option or API field.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+"""Unit tests for the Qwen3-VL reranker path in serving_rerank.py.
+
+The VL reranker scores each document with its own generate request. These
+tests check that all documents of a rerank request are in flight at the
+same time (so the scheduler can batch them), that scores still line up with
+the input order when requests finish out of order, and that prompt
+logprobs are not requested.
+"""
+
+from sglang.test.test_utils import maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()  # must precede any import that pulls in sgl_kernel
+
+import asyncio
+import math
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import V1RerankReqInput
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.serving_rerank import OpenAIServingRerank
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=4, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+YES_ID = 10
+NO_ID = 20
+# Detected as a Qwen3-VL reranker template: reranker phrase + vision token.
+TEMPLATE = (
+    'Answer can only be "yes" or "no". <|vision_start|>'
+    "{% for x in document %}{{ x.text }}{% endfor %}"
+)
+
+
+class _Tokenizer:
+    chat_template = TEMPLATE
+
+    def encode(self, text, **kwargs):
+        return [{"yes": YES_ID, "no": NO_ID}[text]]
+
+
+class _TokenizerManager:
+    server_args = object()
+    tokenizer = _Tokenizer()
+    model_config = SimpleNamespace(
+        is_generation=True, model_path="Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B"
+    )
+
+    def __init__(self, p_yes_by_doc, delay_by_doc=None, wait_for=None):
+        self.p_yes_by_doc = p_yes_by_doc
+        self.delay_by_doc = delay_by_doc or {}
+        # When set, each request waits until this many requests are in flight.
+        self.wait_for = wait_for
+        self.requests = []
+        self.in_flight = 0
+        self.max_in_flight = 0
+        self._all_started = asyncio.Event()
+
+    def _document(self, request):
+        # The rendered prompt ends with the document text.
+        return next(d for d in self.p_yes_by_doc if request.text.endswith(d))
+
+    async def generate_request(self, request, raw_request):
+        doc = self._document(request)
+        self.requests.append(request)
+        self.in_flight += 1
+        self.max_in_flight = max(self.max_in_flight, self.in_flight)
+        if self.wait_for is not None:
+            if len(self.requests) == self.wait_for:
+                self._all_started.set()
+            # A serial implementation never starts the next request, so bound
+            # the wait instead of hanging the test.
+            await asyncio.wait_for(self._all_started.wait(), timeout=1.0)
+        await asyncio.sleep(self.delay_by_doc.get(doc, 0))
+        self.in_flight -= 1
+        p_yes = self.p_yes_by_doc[doc]
+        labels = [
+            (math.log(p_yes), YES_ID, "yes"),
+            (math.log(1 - p_yes), NO_ID, "no"),
+        ]
+        # Answer whichever logprob form the handler asked for.
+        meta_info = {}
+        if request.top_logprobs_num:
+            meta_info["output_top_logprobs"] = [labels]
+        if request.token_ids_logprob:
+            meta_info["output_token_ids_logprobs"] = [labels]
+        yield {"meta_info": meta_info}
+
+
+def _rerank(manager, documents):
+    handler = OpenAIServingRerank(manager)
+    request = V1RerankReqInput(
+        query="query", documents=documents, return_documents=True
+    )
+
+    async def run():
+        return await handler._handle_non_streaming_request(request, request, None)
+
+    return asyncio.run(run())
+
+
+class TestServingRerankVLConcurrency(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_documents_are_in_flight_together(self):
+        docs = [f"doc{i}" for i in range(4)]
+        manager = _TokenizerManager({doc: 0.5 for doc in docs}, wait_for=len(docs))
+
+        result = _rerank(manager, docs)
+
+        self.assertIsInstance(result, list)
+        self.assertEqual(len(result), len(docs))
+        self.assertEqual(manager.max_in_flight, len(docs))
+
+    def test_scores_follow_input_order_when_finished_out_of_order(self):
+        p_yes = {"doc0": 0.9, "doc1": 0.6, "doc2": 0.3, "doc3": 0.1}
+        # The first document finishes last.
+        delay = {"doc0": 0.03, "doc1": 0.02, "doc2": 0.01, "doc3": 0.0}
+        manager = _TokenizerManager(p_yes, delay_by_doc=delay)
+
+        result = _rerank(manager, list(p_yes))
+
+        self.assertEqual([r.index for r in result], [0, 1, 2, 3])
+        for r in result:
+            self.assertEqual(r.document, f"doc{r.index}")
+            self.assertAlmostEqual(r.score, p_yes[r.document])
+
+    def test_requests_skip_prompt_logprobs(self):
+        docs = ["doc0", "doc1"]
+        manager = _TokenizerManager({doc: 0.5 for doc in docs})
+
+        _rerank(manager, docs)
+
+        self.assertEqual(len(manager.requests), len(docs))
+        for request in manager.requests:
+            self.assertTrue(request.return_logprob)
+            self.assertEqual(request.logprob_start_len, -1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
